chunks: And in the narration of Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Umar ibn Yazid: [it is] like that, and he added to it: 'the mosque of Basra'.
ai.seo_question: Which mosques are specified for i'tikaf in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* reinforces the permissibility of i'tikaf by explicitly including the mosque of Basra, reflecting the early Shia scholarly practice of validating major urban mosques for spiritual retreat. It highlights the continuity of the chain of transmission (isnad) through key figures like al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, underscoring the reliability of this specific legal extension within the Shia jurisprudential tradition.
